create_render.description: Render a video or image from one of your Creatomate templates, swapping in your own text and media. Rendering is asynchronous, so use Get a render to pick up the finished file.
create_render.name: create_render

parameters.description: The template to render, as returned by List templates. It's also the ID shown in the Creatomate template editor's URL.
parameters.name: template_id

parameters.description: What to change in the template, keyed by element name -- for example {"Text-1": "Now 20% off", "Video-1": "https://example.com/clip.mp4"}. Use Get a template to see which element names it has.
parameters.name: modifications

parameters.description: Scale the output relative to the template's own resolution. 1 is full size, 0.5 is half. Between 0.1 and 10.
parameters.name: render_scale

parameters.description: Optional. Scale the output down so it is no wider than this, in pixels.
parameters.name: max_width

parameters.description: Optional. Scale the output down so it is no taller than this, in pixels.
parameters.name: max_height

parameters.description: Optional. Creatomate calls this URL once the render finishes or fails, so you don't have to poll for it.
parameters.name: webhook_url

parameters.description: Optional. Any text to attach to the render and pass back to your webhook, such as a campaign ID.
parameters.name: metadata

duration.description: Length of the output in seconds, for videos only

error_message.description: Why the render failed, when it did. Empty otherwise.

file_size.description: Size of the output file in bytes

frame_rate.description: Frames per second of the output, for videos only

height.description: Height of the output in pixels

render_id.description: The render's ID. Use with Get a render to poll for the result.

render_status.description: How far the render has got: 'planned', 'waiting', 'transcribing', 'rendering', 'succeeded', or 'failed'. Rendering is asynchronous, so a freshly created render is usually not 'succeeded' yet.

renders.description: Every render this request queued. Usually one, but a template can fan out into several outputs.

duration.description: Length of the output in seconds, for videos only

error_message.description: Why the render failed, when it did. Empty otherwise.

file_size.description: Size of the output file in bytes

frame_rate.description: Frames per second of the output, for videos only

height.description: Height of the output in pixels

render_id.description: The render's ID. Use with Get a render to poll for the result.

render_status.description: How far the render has got: 'planned', 'waiting', 'transcribing', 'rendering', 'succeeded', or 'failed'. Rendering is asynchronous, so a freshly created render is usually not 'succeeded' yet.

snapshot_url.description: Link to a still frame taken from the video, for videos only

template_id.description: ID of the template this was rendered from

url.description: Direct download link to the finished file. Only populated once the render has succeeded.

width.description: Width of the output in pixels

get_template.description: Look up one template, including the RenderScript source that tells you which element names a render can modify.
get_template.name: get_template

parameters.description: The template to render, as returned by List templates. It's also the ID shown in the Creatomate template editor's URL.
parameters.name: template_id

name.description: The template's name in your project

source.description: The template's full RenderScript. Read the element names out of this to know what Create a render can change.

tags.description: The tags the template is filed under

template_id.description: The template's ID. Use with Create a render.

updated_at.description: When the template was last changed
